params.description: Reference to a secret defined on the environment, written {"$envSecret": "<shortName>"}. The environment owns the value: the component only resolves and publishes it, and deleting the component leaves the secret in place. Preferred over 'secretValue'; when both are set, this one wins. Fails when no environment secret has that short name.

Name under which 'secretValue' is stored in the environment secret store. When unset, the component id. Ignored when 'secret' references an environment secret, which keeps its own name. Changing it writes a new secret and revokes the readers' grants on the old one.

Raw secret value (legacy) that the component stores in the environment secret store under 'secretName', granting read access to the custom workloads linked to it. Required when 'secret' is not set; deleting the component deletes the stored secret.
Deprecated: id of the Kubernetes cluster component to deploy into. Used only when the component declares no dependency on a Kubernetes cluster; declare that dependency instead.

Ports Traefik listens on, each a map {name, port, exposedPort, protocol, isTlsEnabled, isHttpsRedirected} or a 'name:port' string. exposedPort defaults to port, protocol to tcp (tcp or udp), isTlsEnabled to true (in the string form, true only for https and websecure) and isHttpsRedirected to false. Entries without a name or port are skipped and none left fails the component; a name must be a valid Kubernetes port name (at most 15 characters) and cannot be 'traefik', which the agent reserves.
Name of the environment secret the forward-auth service signs its session cookies with. Required together with the other three OIDC keys; a name that resolves to no secret counts as unset.

Fully qualified host name the Traefik dashboard and API route (and the /_oauth callback when OIDC is on) answers on. When unset, that route matches an empty host, which no request carries: the dashboard and API are unreachable, and so is the /_oauth callback this route serves.
Static IP address requested for Traefik's LoadBalancer Service (loadBalancerIP). The address must already be reserved for the cluster; when unset, the cloud provider assigns one.

derived.note: defaults to the component id when absent

params.description: Kubernetes namespace Traefik is deployed into. When unset, the component id, which must then be a valid DNS-1123 label (at most 63 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens).
Client id of the OIDC application registered for this gateway. Required together with the other three OIDC keys.

Name of the environment secret holding the OIDC client secret; the raw secret is never a parameter. Required together with the other three OIDC keys; a name that resolves to no secret counts as unset.

Issuer URL of the OpenID Connect provider that protects the routes through forward authentication. OIDC is enabled only when oidcIssuerUrl, oidcClientId, oidcClientSecretId and forwardAuthSecretId are all set; setting only some of them fails the component.

HSTS security-headers middleware: a map {active, stsSeconds, stsIncludeSubdomains, stsPreload, stsForce}. When unset, the middleware is applied with stsSeconds 63072000 (two years) and the three flags true; any key left out of the map takes that same value, and active=false removes the middleware.

TLS certificates Traefik serves, each a map {certSecretId, keySecretId, isDefault} naming the environment secrets that hold the base64-encoded PEM certificate and its private key. Entries missing either id are skipped; a named secret that does not exist fails the component. When none is marked isDefault, the first one is the default certificate.

TLS options of the entry points, as {supportedTlsVersions, supportedCiphers}: supportedTlsVersions lists TLS_1_0, TLS_1_1, TLS_1_2 or TLS_1_3 (the lowest becomes the minimum version; any other value fails the component), supportedCiphers lists cipher-suite names as Go's crypto/tls spells them (e.g. TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256). Each half left unset keeps its default: TLS 1.2 and 1.3, with a fixed list of ECDHE and TLS 1.3 AES-GCM / ChaCha20 suites.

Distributed tracing, as {jaeger: {collectorEndpoint, localAgentPort, localAgentUrlPath}}. When jaeger is set without a collectorEndpoint, the endpoint is taken from the Jaeger component this gateway links to with link type JaegerTracing, and the component fails when there is no such link. When unset, tracing is off.

params.description: OCI availability domain the instance is launched in, by its full tenancy-specific name as OCI lists it for the region. Applied when the instance is created.

OCI compartment the component's resource is created in, as {parentId, name, description?}: parentId is the OCID of the parent compartment or tenancy, name the compartment's name. The compartment is looked up under parentId and created there when absent (description defaults to 'Standard compartment'). Required for a new component; nothing is assumed. A deployed component without it is kept in the compartment its resource lives in, with a warning. Offers that run on a Kubernetes cluster do not read it.

Workload identity attached to the VM, so software on it reaches cloud services without keys. Each cloud reads only its own fields: GCP 'serviceAccount' (email) and 'scopes' (cloud-platform when unset), AWS 'instanceProfile' (IAM instance-profile name), Azure 'managedIdentity' ("system" or a user-assigned identity resource id), OCI 'instancePrincipal' (true) and 'policyStatements' (IAM policy statements granted to the instance's dynamic group). When unset, no identity is requested here; one the VM's links need is created by the agent.

OCID of the image the instance boots from (ocid1.image...). Required to create: a new instance without it is refused; a deployed one keeps its image, with a warning. Applied when the instance is created; changing it does not rebuild an existing one.
SSH public key(s) in OpenSSH format, set as the instance's ssh_authorized_keys metadata. When unset, no key is installed. Applied when the instance is created.
Memory in GB of a Flex shape. Wins over size. Refused with a fixed shape. When neither it nor size is set, 16 GB per OCPU. Applied when the instance is created.
OCPUs of a Flex shape (1 OCPU = 2 vCPUs). Wins over size. Refused with a fixed shape. When neither it nor size is set, 1 on a declared Flex shape. Applied when the instance is created.

OCI shape (e.g. VM.Standard.E4.Flex). Wins over size. Applied when the instance is created. Set it or size: a new instance with neither is refused, as no VM size is assumed; size maps to VM.Standard.E4.Flex. An existing instance keeps its shape.

Vendor-neutral VM size: small (1-2 vCPU, 1-2 GiB, burstable), medium (2 vCPU, 8 GiB), large (4 vCPU, 16 GiB), xlarge (8 vCPU, 32 GiB). Mapped to this offer's own size key when that key is not set; an explicitly set vendor size key wins (a contradiction is published as a contract warning). Applies when the VM is created only: changing it never resizes or recreates an existing VM.
Startup script (cloud-init) as raw text; the agent base64-encodes it into the instance's user_data metadata. When unset, none. Applied when the instance is created.

Whether the load balancer is private (no public IP). Defaults to private for a new load balancer. Fixed at creation: an existing load balancer keeps its exposure, and declaring the opposite is refused, as is a value other than true or false.

OCI load balancer shape name: flexible, which OCI creates new load balancers on and which takes minimumBandwidthInMbps and maximumBandwidthInMbps, or a legacy fixed-bandwidth shape (10Mbps, 100Mbps, 400Mbps, 8000Mbps) where the tenancy still accepts one. None is assumed: a new load balancer without it is refused. Applied when the load balancer is created; an existing one keeps its shape.

Upper bound, in Mbps, of the flexible shape's bandwidth (10 to 8000, at least minimumBandwidthInMbps). Required with lbType flexible, together with minimumBandwidthInMbps; no range is assumed. Used only with the flexible shape, when the load balancer is created.

Lower bound, in Mbps, of the flexible shape's bandwidth (10 to 8000). Required with lbType flexible, together with maximumBandwidthInMbps; no range is assumed. Used only with the flexible shape, when the load balancer is created.

Free-text description of the security group. When unset, the component id. Not sent to OCI: the network security group is named after the component id.

Outbound rules: [{protocol?, fromPort?, toPort?, sourceCidr | destCidr | sourceComponentId}]; the CIDR or component is the destination. An omitted toPort means the single port fromPort. Unset leaves the group's egress untouched; declared (even empty) the rules are exactly these. On OCI the rules are the network security group's egress rules; it has no egress until some is declared.

Inbound rules: [{protocol?, fromPort?, toPort?, sourceCidr | sourceComponentId}]. protocol defaults to tcp; an omitted toPort means the single port fromPort. A rule with neither sourceCidr nor sourceComponentId is skipped; a sourceComponentId resolves to that component's managed security group. The group's ingress rules are exactly these: unset or empty removes every ingress rule.

Whether to run the Fractal-built PostgreSQL image bundling the Apache AGE graph extension, preloaded as a shared library. When unset, false. Requires PostgreSQL 17.2, the only version with a published AGE image: a new cluster on any other version is refused, and a deployed one keeps the image it runs, with a warning. Toggling it on a running cluster swaps the image with a rolling update.

CPU limit of each PostgreSQL instance, as a Kubernetes quantity (cores or millicores). When unset, 1. Applied when the cluster is created; on a running cluster a change is applied only together with a change of instances or of the PostgreSQL image.

CPU requested by each PostgreSQL instance, as a Kubernetes quantity (cores, or millicores such as 500m). When unset, 500m. Applied when the cluster is created; on a running cluster a change is applied only together with a change of instances or of the PostgreSQL image.
Name of the database created when the cluster is bootstrapped. When unset, app. Bootstrap runs once: changing it later does not create or rename a database (use a CnpgDatabase component for more).
PostgreSQL role that owns the bootstrap database; CloudNativePG creates it with a generated password. When unset, app. Used only when the cluster is bootstrapped.

Whether CloudNativePG enables the postgres superuser and publishes its password in a Kubernetes secret. When unset, false. Applied when the cluster is created; on a running cluster a change is applied only together with a change of instances or of the PostgreSQL image.
Number of PostgreSQL instances in the CloudNativePG cluster: one primary, the rest streaming replicas, spread across zones when possible. When unset, 3. A change is applied to a running cluster.

Memory limit of each PostgreSQL instance, as a Kubernetes quantity (e.g. 1Gi). When unset, 1Gi. Applied when the cluster is created; on a running cluster a change is applied only together with a change of instances or of the PostgreSQL image.

Memory requested by each PostgreSQL instance, as a Kubernetes quantity (e.g. 512Mi). When unset, 512Mi. Applied when the cluster is created; on a running cluster a change is applied only together with a change of instances or of the PostgreSQL image.

derived.note: defaults to the component id when absent

params.description: Kubernetes namespace the resources are created in; created when missing. When unset, the component id, which must then be a valid DNS-1123 label (at most 63 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens).

PostgreSQL version, used as the tag of the ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/postgresql image (e.g. 17.2). Takes precedence over 'version'; when neither is set, 17.2. A running cluster only moves within its major version: a different major is kept at the deployed one, because a major upgrade needs a migration. With age=true only 17.2 is available.

Kubernetes storage class of the data volumes. When unset, the cluster's default storage class. Applied when the cluster is created; on a running cluster a change is applied only together with a change of instances or of the PostgreSQL image.

Size of each instance's data volume, as a Kubernetes quantity (e.g. 10Gi). When unset, 10Gi. Applied when the cluster is created; on a running cluster a change is applied only together with a change of instances or of the PostgreSQL image.

PostgreSQL version as declared by the blueprint component, used when 'postgresqlVersion' is not set. Applies only when the cluster is created: a running cluster keeps its deployed version unless 'postgresqlVersion' asks for another one.

derived.note: the CnpgCluster component this database depends on

params.description: Component id of the CnpgCluster, in the same Live System, that hosts the database. When unset, the CnpgCluster this component depends on; with neither the database fails. It waits until that cluster is Active.
Deprecated. Id of the Kubernetes cluster component to deploy on, read only when this component declares no dependency on a Kubernetes cluster. Declare that dependency instead.

Name of the PostgreSQL database created in the CloudNativePG cluster. Required to create: a new database without one is refused; set it to the database name your application connects to. Used only when the database is created: an existing database is never changed, and one declared without it is kept, with a warning.

derived.note: the role the CnpgCluster bootstraps (its databaseOwner)

params.description: Existing PostgreSQL role that owns the database. When unset, the role the CnpgCluster bootstraps (that cluster's databaseOwner). Used only when the database is created: an existing database is never changed.
Character encoding of the database, as PostgreSQL names it (e.g. UTF8). When unset, UTF8. Used only when the database is created: an existing database is never changed.

Character classification locale (LC_CTYPE) of the database, the Database resource's localeCType; it must be a locale the PostgreSQL image provides. When unset, the cluster's default. Used only when the database is created: CloudNativePG refuses to change it afterwards.

Collation locale (LC_COLLATE) of the database, the Database resource's localeCollate, e.g. en_US.UTF-8; it must be a locale the PostgreSQL image provides. When unset, the cluster's default. Used only when the database is created: CloudNativePG refuses to change it afterwards.

derived.note: defaults to the component id when absent

params.description: Kubernetes namespace of the database resource. Always the namespace of its CnpgCluster: when unset, that one is used, and a different value fails the component, because the operator only adopts a database in its cluster's namespace.

Reference to a secret defined on the environment, written {"$envSecret": "<shortName>"}. The environment owns the value: the component only resolves and publishes it, and deleting the component leaves the secret in place. Preferred over 'secretValue'; when both are set, this one wins. Fails when no environment secret has that short name.

Name under which 'secretValue' is stored in the environment secret store. When unset, the component id. Ignored when 'secret' references an environment secret, which keeps its own name. Changing it writes a new secret and revokes the readers' grants on the old one.

Raw secret value (legacy) that the component stores in the environment secret store under 'secretName', granting read access to the custom workloads linked to it. Required when 'secret' is not set; deleting the component deletes the stored secret.
